html:
In 1421 the Yongle Emperor moved the capital of Ming China from Nanjing on the Yangtze to Beijing in the north. The Forbidden City was built for the move.

Yongle had seized the throne from his nephew in a civil war, starting from his own base at Beijing. The north also faced the Mongols, the main threat to the dynasty. To feed a capital far from the rice lands, the Grand Canal was rebuilt so grain barges could come up from the south.

In the same years Yongle sent Zheng He's fleets across the Indian Ocean. Soon after his death the voyages stopped, the fleets rotted and the state turned to the Mongol frontier and the Great Wall. The historian Fernand Braudel saw the move inland as China turning its back on the sea, just before Europeans began their own oceanic expansion. Others point out that Chinese private trade by sea went on and grew.
sum: In 1421 the Yongle Emperor moved the capital of Ming China from Nanjing on the Yangtze to Beijing in the north. The Forbidden City was built for the move.
